title: Compact Prefill Replayer and Quant Catalog
author: Maya K. Chen
release_notes: Adds a prefill replay utility and a compact quant catalog with compatibility scoring. New CLI for snapshot exports, tenant-default migration, and backend telemetry hooks. No public API breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR introduces two complementary pieces to improve automated cost defaults across tenants: (1) a lightweight Prefill Replayer that snapshots compact prefill/KV-cache signals from live traffic, replays them offline in a batched warmstart simulator, and emits profile recommendations (batching + cache window defaults); (2) a Compact Quant Catalog service that stores small metadata-first quantization variants and compatibility scores to guide safe default selection for tenant workloads. The goal is to produce robust, tenant-specific defaults for batching/cache/quantization with observability and a non-destructive migration path.

High-level design:
- Prefill snapshotter: agent in runtime that emits compressed prefill fingerprints (hashed token prefixes, sequence-length histograms, and minimal KV-cache signature) at configurable sample rates. Snapshots are intentionally lossy and privacy-preserving (no plain-text prefixes retained).
- Replayer/simulator: a lightweight offline harness that consumes snapshots, groups them into representative warmstart sets, and runs a fast-path token-throughput and latency emulation to estimate per-tenant cost/latency under candidate defaults. Produces metrics: expected tokens saved, latency delta, and failure risk score.
- Compact Quant Catalog: a metadata service (small Dynamo-style table) that registers quant variants with coverage vectors (seq_len buckets, model-arch tags) and a precomputed compatibility score (0-1) derived from small regression tests. The Replayer consults the catalog to simulate fallback quant behaviors and recommend safe quant tiers.
- Migration & CLI: add 'redwood-econ snapshot export|replay|apply' CLI to produce dry-run recommendations and an opt-in migration step for tenant defaults. Includes a 7-day shadow-run mode option.

Checklist (what's included):
- [x] Runtime snapshot emitter + sampling config (env var + tenant throttle).
- [x] Offline replayer harness with batching and warmstart simulation.
- [x] Compact Quant Catalog schema + registration API and seed entries for existing quant tiers.
- [x] CLI for export/replay/dryrun/migrate with shadow-run support.
- [x] Unit and integration tests for replayer and catalog scoring.
- [x] Telemetry hooks (prefill.profile.* metrics and quant.catalog.*).
- [x] Docs: developer guide for snapshot privacy, migration playbook, and runbook for troubleshooting.

Commits (summary):
- feat(prefill): compact snapshot emitter + sampling config (maya/commit/1)
- feat(replayer): warmstart group builder + fast-path simulator (maya/commit/2)
- feat(quant-catalog): metadata service, schema, seed data and registration API (maya/commit/3)
- feat(cli): redwood-econ snapshot/replay/migrate commands + shadow-run flag (maya/commit/4)
- test(prefill/replayer): add unit/integration tests and CI matrix (maya/commit/5)
- docs: migration playbook and privacy note (maya/commit/6)
- fix(ci): flaky e2e warmstart test tolerance increased (maya/commit/7)

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/prefill/snapshotter.py - new: compact emitter; sampling config and tenant opt-in. Snippet: 'emit_compact_snapshot(hash_prefix(pfx), seq_hist, kv_sig, tenant_id_masked)'.
- tools/replayer/replayer.py - new: grouping logic, fast-path latency/cost estimator, result exporter (JSON).
- services/quant_catalog/api.py - new: register/query endpoints, compatibility scoring code.
- cli/redwood_econ.py - new: snapshot/replay/migrate commands and flags.
- infra/seed/quant_catalog_seed.json - new: seed entries for q4/q8/q8_4 variants with coverage vectors.
- docs/playbooks/prefill-migration.md - new: runbook and shadow-run instructions.
- tests/replayer/test_replayer.py - new: deterministic scenarios and mocks.
- tests/ci/e2e_warmstart.yml - updated: increase tolerance and add retry for flaky case.

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego: "Nice focused scope. Two asks: (1) make sure emitter sampling is low overhead and opt-in per-tenant; (2) add a TTL and rolling compaction for the catalog seed table."
- Maya: "Addressed: emitter runs on low-priority worker thread, sampling default 0.05 (configurable), and catalog entries have default ttl_days=90 with compaction job in infra/cron."
- Priya: "Can we quantify risk when a quant fallback might degrade accuracy? Need a 'failure risk score' in output so SRE/product can decide."
- Maya: "Added a risk_score field in replayer output derived from small evals and sequence-length mismatch heuristics; documented thresholds in playbook."
- Evan: "Tests look good; one integration flake in e2e warmstart caused CI rerun."
- Evan (approve): "Approve after CI green and small doc tweak."

CI summary:
- Unit tests: pass (matrix: py3.9, py3.10)
- Integration tests: pass (replayer harness mocked against small seed)
- E2E warmstart sim: flaky on first run (timing sensitivity) -> tolerance bump + rerun -> pass
- Lint/Formatter: pass

Migration notes and rollout plan:
1) Deploy catalog service and seed data to staging.
2) Start snapshot emitter in staging with sampling=0.1 and run replayer to produce recommendations for a week.
3) Run CLI in dry-run mode to validate recommendations per-tenant.
4) For low-risk tenants (risk_score < 0.15) enable shadow-run migrate option for 7 days to verify metrics.
5) After shadow-run, apply defaults with canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and monitor prefill.profile.* and latency/trace dashboards.

Telemetry and observability:
- Metrics exported: prefill.profile.snapshots_emitted, prefill.replayer.replays, prefill.replayer.recommendations{outcome}, quant.catalog.query_count, quant.catalog.compatibility_histogram.
- Logs: snapshot IDs and masked tenant tags; replayer debug traces for failing scenarios.
- Alerting: add an alert if applied recommendations cause median tail latency increase > 10% over baseline during canary.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- No customer-facing API breaking changes.
- Defaults are only applied via opt-in migration CLI or via explicit policy.
- All emitted snapshots are hashed and designed to avoid retaining sensitive text. Details and privacy rationale in docs/playbooks/prefill-migration.md.

Testing done:
- Unit tests cover emitter sampling and grouping heuristics.
- Integration tests run the replayer against seeded quant variants and assert expected cost delta sign.
- Small perf harness validates emitter overhead < 1% CPU increase on a production-like worker.
- Manual shadow-run performed on staging for tenant demo-account-42 for 72 hours; observed ~9% token cost reduction with no latency regressions.

Follow-ups (future PRs):
- Add a lightweight explainability report tying a recommended change to a small set of representative snapshots.
- Extend quant catalog to add a small compressed diffs artifact for quick accuracy regressions.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged into main on 2026-03-05 after CI green and approvals from Diego, Priya, Evan.

If there are questions about running the CLI or interpreting the 'risk_score' thresholds, see docs/playbooks/prefill-migration.md or ping @maya.
